Root cause of that asymmetry is in the delivered source and is documented there, not accidental: src/game/simulation.js:34-35 derives elapsedMs and score from the raw monotonic delta, src/game/score.js:12-15 is Math.floor(elapsedMs * 0.01), and PHYSICS.maxStepSeconds 0.05 (src/game/run-state.js:29-30) clamps only the physics step, with the comment that a backgrounded tab must not teleport the character. simulation.js:23-24 states the asymmetry outright.

Correctness split: the monotonic source makes the behaviour correct against AC-21 (monotonic, wall-clock-change safe), AC-20 (sessionLengthMs within 250 ms of externally observed run duration - background time genuinely is part of that duration, so subtracting it via visibilitychange would break AC-20 as written) and AC-08 (integer, starts at zero, never decreases). It does not make the score a measure of play: the score measures wall-clock time since run start, and hidden time accrues at the full rate with zero collision risk, reachable by Ctrl+Tab with no tooling. Recorded as a property, not as an AC failure.

knownRisks: L-01 - One platform premise is reasoned, not measured. That Chromium suspends or heavily throttles requestAnimationFrame for a hidden tab while performance.now() keeps advancing is documented platform behaviour and is the premise of the frame schedule used; it was not observed in a browser here. What was measured is the delivered code's response to that schedule. Browser-side confirmation belongs to WS-10 and is not claimed.

L-02 - The background-gap check is a harness, not the game. It drives advanceRun/markRunStart directly with an injected deterministic random source; it does not run main.js, the state machine, the renderer or the HUD. Sufficient for the claim made, since score and elapsed time are computed entirely inside those two functions, but not a substitute for a browser-tier observation after a real tab switch.

L-03 - Word-boundary matching materially changes these scan results. A plain substring scan reports expo 45 times in src/ (inside 'export') and freeze 41 times as though a Page Lifecycle handler existed (all Object.freeze). Both were disambiguated. Recorded so a later reader running a naive grep does not rediscover the discrepancy as a finding.

L-04 - The scan covers the repository as it stands, and node_modules does not exist yet. WS-12 has not recorded a run, so there is no root package.json and no installed dependency tree. If ENG-12 later adds dev dependencies, the SBOM view of that is WS-09's, not this workstream's.

L-05 - The background-time scoring property is recorded, not accepted. ENG-05 has no authority to accept a product risk and did not. DEC-20260809-001 covers deliberate client-side score forgery bounded to Units 1 and 2; it does not address time-derived accrual while hidden, and this record must not be cited as extending it. It is also not recorded as an AC failure - it satisfies AC-08, AC-20 and AC-21 as written.

L-06 - not_applicable is scoped to Unit 1 at this revision and is not a standing judgement that Dino Dash will never have a client. Units 2 through 5 are not contracted and nothing here pre-clears them.

R-05 - Open for a later unit: whether the score is meant to measure play or wall-clock time must be settled before Unit 3 puts these values in a shared table. If the answer is play, the obvious visibilitychange fix changes the meaning of sessionLengthMs, whose name, type and unit are frozen by ADR-003 section 6 (additive fields only), and would need re-checking against AC-20's 250 ms tolerance. This is a product question, not a delivery detail.

R-06 - Open for a later unit: no test covers score accrual across a frame gap; only the physics clamp is covered. Whatever is decided above, a unit-tier test driving advanceRun across a gap is needed, and needs no browser.

R-07 - Open for a later unit: AC-24's playable offline means the loaded page keeps working with the network off, not that the game is available without the static origin. With no service worker and no cache manifest, a cold load still requires the server. A PWA route would introduce a persistent cache and collide directly with AC-22 and AC-23, so it is a product-direction question behind the human product_direction_or_priority gate, not an engineering choice.

R-08 - Open for a later unit: there is no upgrade surface at all. window.dinoDash.version === 1 is a page-local constant on a read-only observation accessor, not an application version; there is no update channel and no cached older copy to supersede. If touch is ever added it must be additive to src/input/, since AC-12 requires the keyboard path to remain complete on its own, and AC-15 would require any new affordance to be named on screen.
